name: Southern Ionics
what_it_is: A family-owned maker of liquid inorganic chemicals founded in 1980. It produces aluminum chemicals (sodium aluminate, alum, aluminum chloride, PHOS-SORB), sulfur reducing agents (sodium bisulfite, sulfite, thiosulfate), AQUA-CAT aqua ammonia and dried alumina trihydrate (ATH) at about 10 plants across the Southeast, Gulf Coast and Maryland. Water/wastewater treatment is one important outlet among several; refinery-catalyst, zeolite and TiO2 feedstocks, power-plant NOx control, pulp and ATH fillers are the others.
primary_category: Specialty / intermediate chemicals (water is a minor outlet)
bluntly: Mostly a merchant inorganic intermediates supplier. An estimated ~27% of revenue is water treatment (alum/aluminate coagulants, PHOS-SORB, bisulfite dechlorination). The bulk is sodium aluminate for FCC catalysts, zeolites and TiO2, aqua ammonia for SCR NOx control, and ATH.
ultimate_parent: Southern Ionics Incorporated (privately held; founder Milton O. Sundbeck Jr., Chairman & CEO)
prior_owners: None. Founder-owned since it was established in 1980 in Mobile, AL (the founder started in his garage).
total_revenue_basis: ESTIMATE (no disclosure). The company states it has 350+ employees. 350 x ~$500k revenue per employee (liquid inorganic producer with commodity pass-through in aqua ammonia and ATH) gives ~$175M. Plausible range $110-240M. Vendor data points are low-quality and bracket the low end: Buzzfile ~$89.9M (with 260 employees, an old count), ZoomInfo/RocketReach $106M, and IncFact '>$500M' (not credible). Prior pass used $230M (350 x $650k). Revised down because per-employee productivity at 10 small liquid plants plus an owned truck/rail fleet is more likely $400-600k.
ebitda_basis: Estimate - ~14% margin on $175M estimated revenue. This is the midpoint of the 10-18% range for merchant liquid inorganics (alum/aluminate/bisulfite), blended down for pass-through aqua ammonia and ATH resale and up for specialty catalyst-grade aluminate and PHOS-SORB. No credit docs, rating reports or deal disclosures exist (the company has no PE or public debt).

profile_md:
## Southern Ionics Incorporated (West Point, MS)

**Bottom line:** Southern Ionics is a founder-owned merchant producer of liquid inorganic chemicals. We estimate revenue at ~$175M and EBITDA at ~$25M; both are estimates because nothing is disclosed. Water treatment is a real but minority outlet at roughly a quarter of sales, or ~$45M of US water revenue. The company is best understood as a Gulf/Southeast supplier of **aluminum, sulfur and ammonia intermediates**. Its biggest customers are refinery-catalyst, zeolite and TiO2 makers, power plants running SCR NOx control, and paper mills. Municipalities buying coagulants, phosphorus-removal products and dechlorination agents are a secondary customer base.

### Business overview
SII makes five product families:
- **Aluminum chemistries:** sodium aluminate in several strengths, including papermakers' grade; aluminum sulfate (alum), including low-iron grades; aluminum chloride; and branded PHOS-SORB, FLUOR-SORB and pH-SORB.
- **Sulfur chemistries:** sodium bisulfite, sulfite and thiosulfate solutions, and SI-NOCHLOR-T2.
- **AQUA-CAT ammonium hydroxide.**
- **Dried alumina trihydrate (ATH).**
- **Smaller lines:** zirconium chemicals (Zirconic), and high-purity alumina since a 2023 pilot.

The company says it is the "largest North American producer of high-quality aluminum chemicals" and holds NSF/ANSI 60 and ISO 9001 certification. It runs its own tank-truck and rail-car fleets, which matters in a business where freight is a large share of delivered cost.

### History and ownership
Milton O. Sundbeck Jr. founded the company in 1980 in Mobile, AL, famously starting in his garage with one delivery driver. It later moved to West Point, MS. The company is privately held and family-owned, with no PE sponsor and no public debt. Sundbeck remains Chairman and CEO. Joseph J. Stevens III, a 22-year SII veteran and former chemist, became President and COO in July 2022, a sign that succession is being put in place.

In the 2010s SII diversified upstream. It invested more than $100M in **Southern Ionics Minerals**, a titanium/zircon mineral-sands mine and processing plant at Offerman, GA that opened in 2015 with ~140 employees. It sold that business to Chemours in August 2019 at an undisclosed price. The sale took SII back to a pure chemicals business, but it also means older vendor employee and revenue figures may mix in the mining operation.

### Products and chemistries
- **Aluminum chemicals:** made in-house from ATH. SII buys wet-cake ATH (including via a partnership with Atlantic Alumina at Gramercy, LA), dries it at its Lake Charles port facility, and converts it at roughly seven aluminum plants. Uses include FCC catalyst, zeolite and TiO2 manufacture, pharmaceuticals, paper sizing, and water/wastewater coagulation. PHOS-SORB is the growth product. SII describes shifting from the collapsing newsprint market to municipal and industrial phosphorus removal, where one aluminate product can replace two chemicals and cut treatment cost by 30-60%. The company cites 40 completed trials heading toward 100+ customers.
- **Sulfur chemicals:** made at Pasadena TX, Tuscaloosa AL and Williamsport MD, plus partner sites. They are reducing agents for wastewater dechlorination, boiler oxygen scavenging, ClO2 destruction in pulp mills, flue-gas desulfurization, surfactant synthesis, food and pharma. A **$34M Tuscaloosa expansion** (construction from Q4 2025, operational Q2 2027) adds sodium metabisulfite to replace imports.
- **AQUA-CAT aqua ammonia:** supplied mainly for SCR/SNCR NOx control at power and industrial plants, plus catalyst and chemical uses. SII bought CF Industries' interest in the Houston Ammonia Terminal in 2015 to secure supply.
- **ATH:** also sold as a flame-retardant filler and for fiber-cement board.

### End markets and customers
Our estimated mix:
- Chemicals/petrochem (TiO2, zeolites, synthesis): ~20%
- Power generation (SCR ammonia, FGD): ~17%
- Refining (FCC catalyst feedstocks, refinery NOx control): ~16%
- Municipal drinking water and wastewater: ~21% combined
- Pulp & paper: ~8%
- General manufacturing: ~8%
- Food, pharma, mining (high-purity quartz at Spruce Pine), semis and feed: the remainder

There is no pool or consumer exposure. Customers are concentrated large industrial accounts plus municipal bid business in the Southeast and Gulf.

### Footprint
The HQ is at 579 Commerce St, West Point MS. Plants are at:
- West Point MS
- Augusta GA
- Baton Rouge LA (two)
- Calhoun TN
- Chickasaw AL
- Carlyss/Lake Charles LA
- Lake Charles port (ATH dryers)
- Pasadena TX
- Tuscaloosa AL
- Williamsport MD

R&D sits in Columbus MS and West Point MS, with third-party distribution points in Beaumont, Houston, Tulsa and Cairo OH. The company cites 13 facilities and 350+ employees.

### Financials (all estimates)
No revenue or EBITDA has ever been disclosed.
- **Revenue:** we estimate ~$175M for 2025 (350 employees x ~$500k; range $110-240M). Vendor databases show $90M (Buzzfile) and $106M (ZoomInfo), which we treat as floors. Our prior pass used $230M.
- **Revenue split (estimated):** aluminum chemicals ~40%, aqua ammonia ~25%, sulfur chemicals ~20%, ATH ~12%, other ~3%.
- **Water revenue:** ~$47M, from municipal coagulants/PHOS-SORB, industrial coagulants, bisulfite dechlorination, boiler scavengers and chloramination ammonia. That is ~27% of total and ~$45M in the US.
- **EBITDA:** estimated ~$25M (~14% margin). This is typical for merchant liquid inorganics, helped by specialty catalyst-grade aluminate but diluted by pass-through ammonia and ATH.

### M&A strategy
SII grows mostly organically and through greenfield builds. Its only identified acquisition is the 2015 purchase of CF Industries' indirect 50% interest in Houston Ammonia Terminal L.P. (PotashCorp/Nutrien was the other partner). Its main portfolio move was the 2019 divestiture of mineral sands to Chemours. There are no water-treatment add-ons.

### Competitive position
- **Aluminum chemicals:** SII competes with USALCO, Chemtrade (alum/PAC), Kemira, GEO Specialty Chemicals and Holland Company in coagulants, and with in-house production at catalyst majors in sodium aluminate. Its edge is catalyst-grade aluminate quality and integrated ATH logistics at Gulf ports.
- **Sulfur chemicals:** SII competes with Calabrian, Esseco and imports, and the metabisulfite build targets import substitution.
- **Aqua ammonia:** SII competes with Tanner Industries, Airgas and fertilizer majors.

### Risks
- Coal-plant retirements shrink SCR ammonia demand.
- Refining and FCC catalyst cyclicality.
- Paper-mill closures in the Southeast.
- Customer concentration.
- Hazmat logistics.
- Key-person and succession risk at a founder-led company.

Upside comes from phosphorus-removal regulation (PHOS-SORB), domestic metabisulfite and HPA for batteries.

### What is uncertain
All financials are estimates, and so is the product and end-market split. It is unclear whether SII still owns its HAT stake, and how plant capacity is allocated between catalyst and water grades. A sale by the founder's family to a strategic or PE buyer is plausible but unannounced.
